I am an old woman of sixty years, farming this small maize plot near my compound here in the South East. I have no money for plenty fertilizer, but I will try to buy small NPK if the agro-dealer has it, and I put the household rubbish and goat droppings on the soil like I always do. The seed I will use is the one I kept from last harvest — my own maize seed, because improved seed is costly and I don tire for wahala. I intercrop with cassava and small melon like my mother taught me, and my children help me small-small when they come from town.
